name: Chawal (white rice, raw)
notes: Long-grain, unenriched. Most US white rice is enriched with iron and folic acid, and this record leaves those additions out

name: Atta (whole-wheat flour)
aliases: whole wheat flour|whole-wheat flour|chapati flour|gehun ka atta

name: Maida (refined wheat flour)
aliases: refined flour|refined wheat flour|all-purpose flour|plain flour|white flour

name: Pav (soft white bread roll)
notes: USDA white breads and rolls are enriched with iron and folic acid. UK white flour is fortified with calcium and iron, so this record's calcium, and probably its iron, are higher than in Indian pav. Tagged vegan because the record has 0 g lactose and 0 mg cholesterol, so the analysed rolls held no milk or butter; pav made with milk is veg

name: Toor dal (split pigeon peas)
aliases: arhar dal|tur dal|tuvar dal|togari bele|thuvaram paruppu|split pigeon peas|pigeon pea dal
notes: Split, no seed coat. USDA has only the whole seed

name: Moong dal (split yellow mung beans)
aliases: mung dal|yellow moong dal|split moong|pasi paruppu|hesaru bele|split mung beans
notes: Split, no seed coat. USDA has only the whole bean

name: Urad dal (split skinned black gram)
aliases: udad dal|white urad dal|dhuli urad dal|ulundu|uddina bele|split black gram
notes: Dhuli (washed) urad dal: split, no seed coat. USDA has only the whole bean

name: Chana dal (split chickpeas)
aliases: bengal gram dal|split bengal gram|kadalai paruppu|kadale bele|split chickpeas
notes: Split, no seed coat. Chana dal is split desi chickpea; neither USDA nor CoFID has that, and CoFID's split record is the Kabuli type. USDA has only the whole seed

name: Masoor dal (red lentils)
aliases: masur dal|red lentils|split red lentils|red lentil dal
notes: Pink or red lentils are the dehulled lentils sold as masoor dal

name: Sabut urad (whole black gram)
aliases: whole urad|sabut urad dal|whole black gram|black urad
notes: USDA names Vigna mungo mungo beans

name: Matki (moth beans)
notes: Dry, raw, whole. The record has no fibre value, so available carbohydrate is missing too

name: Sukha matar (dried split peas)
aliases: vatana|sukhi matar|dried split peas|split peas|green split peas
notes: Green split peas, dry, raw. Ghugni and ragda often use whole dried white or yellow peas; a USDA search of SR Legacy and Foundation found no raw record for those. Folate is 15 µg per 100 g as published, far below what USDA's boiled split peas (172429: 65 µg per 100 g at 69.5% water) imply for the dry pea

name: Ghee (clarified butter)
notes: Anhydrous butter oil is ghee by composition. USDA's record named ghee (171314) has no zinc, folate, vitamin A, B12 or vitamin D values and no portions

name: Fresh cream (24% fat)
notes: Indian fresh cream is about 25% fat. USDA's nearest creams are 19% and 31% fat

name: Doodh (whole milk)
notes: 3.25% fat, without added vitamins A and D, because fortification of Indian milk varies by brand

name: Sunflower oil
notes: Linoleic type, the common refined sunflower oil

name: Aloo (potato, peeled)
notes: Flesh only, as Indian dishes use it. USDA SR Legacy has raw potato only with the skin or as skin alone, and the Foundation records without skin have no fibre value, so available carbohydrate would be missing

name: Kachcha kela (raw banana, green plantain)
aliases: raw banana|green banana|green plantain|kachha kela|kanch kola|vazhakkai
notes: USDA green plantain. Indian raw bananas are cooking varieties that may hold more water than this record, in which case kcal and carbohydrate read high

name: Methi (fenugreek leaves)
aliases: fenugreek leaves|methi leaves|fresh methi|menthya soppu|vendhaya keerai

name: Hari mirch (green chilli)
notes: Hot chilli, not green bell pepper

name: Nariyal doodh (coconut milk)
notes: Liquid pressed from grated coconut and water, as made at home

name: Rai (mustard seeds)
notes: USDA lists the seed ground; grinding does not change its composition

name: Lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
notes: Ground red chilli (cayenne), not US chili powder, which is a blend with salt

name: Anda (egg, whole, raw)
notes: Chicken egg, whole, without the shell

name: Rohu (Labeo rohita)
notes: USDA has no rohu. CoFID's rohu record comes from literature sources and does not report calcium, zinc, folate, saturated fat or fibre. Its vitamin A and vitamin D cells are "Tr" (trace), stored as 0. USDA's common carp (171952) has 5.6 g fat per 100 g against 1.4 g here, so it was not used as a stand-in

name: Surmai (king mackerel)
notes: USDA's king mackerel is the Atlantic species (Scomberomorus cavalla). Surmai on Indian coasts is S. commerson, from the same genus; USDA has no record for it

name: Meetha soda (baking soda)
aliases: baking soda|khane ka soda|cooking soda|soda bicarbonate|sodium bicarbonate
